trust_decision.summary: The GraphQL layer decides that a client-supplied GraphQL argument value (here the password of check<Type>Password) is data and may not change the structure of the DQL string that the rewriter builds and sends to the executor. The pinned code interpolates the password raw into checkpwd(pred, "%s").

landing_point.why: The advisory names checkUserPassword. The PasswordQuery case at graphql/resolve/query_rewriter.go:150 leads straight to passwordQuery and to the only fmt.Sprintf with a quoted %s in the rewriter.

fix_sites.entry_point: GraphQL /graphql query check<Type>Password (generated for each type with @secret, graphql/schema/gqlschema.go:2285)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: graphql/admin/current_user.go:30-41 (wrapper that implements resolve.QueryRewriter in the admin package; changed only because the interface changed, so it is not a security site)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the regexp route: DQL regexp literals are /pattern/flags and must not be quoted, and the regexp filter is a separate search feature unrelated to password checking, so a solver will argue it is a different feature with intentionally raw syntax.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Regexp filters must keep emitting an unquoted /pattern/flags literal. Quoting every string with %q or binding it as a variable would break the existing 'All String regexp filters work' rewriting cases and e2e regexp tests. Separately, password values containing quotes, backslashes or unicode must still verify against the stored hash.

O6_input_shapes: single String password argument on check<Type>Password, given inline or as a GraphQL variable; both reach m.ArgValue(name).(string) at graphql/resolve/query_rewriter.go:352

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The GraphQL filter value of a regexp search on a String field is written raw into the DQL @filter(regexp(pred, VALUE)) and is reachable from query<Type>, aggregate<Type>, nested field filters and update/delete mutation filters.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Regexp is a different query type from the password check, and its DQL literal syntax (/re/flags) is deliberately unquoted, so a solver could call it a neighbouring feature that is out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, about 1975 lines away; reached via buildFilter (graphql/resolve/query_rewriter.go:1977) and mutation_rewriter.go:990

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Enum and boolean filter values formatted with %v and no quoting. A sibling could route a free-form String through this branch.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment already treats enums as 'eq(Post.postType, "Question")'. A maintainer adding a new scalar or custom filter could reuse the %v branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Root type(%s) and order or pagination values written raw by AsString. A sibling could pass a client string (for example a dynamic type or orderBy name) through it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: AsString documents that it does not validate (graphql/dgraph/graphquery.go:16-18), and many Attr strings are built with fmt.Sprintf in the rewriter.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: similar_to ef/distance_threshold options formatted with %v. A sibling could be a string-typed option such as a metric name.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Vector-search options are new and still growing, and they are built as raw 'name: value' strings.

O9_family: injection (CWE-943 DQL query injection via string interpolation in the GraphQL-to-DQL rewriter)

O10_build.project_tests: graphql/resolve/query_test.go + query_test.yaml and auth_test.go + auth_query_test.yaml are pure rewriting tests that need no cluster. The e2e tests in graphql/e2e/common need a Dgraph cluster (Docker).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Use strconv.Quote/%q on the password in passwordQuery (correct for that site, because the DQL parser uses strconv.Unquote at dql/parser.go:1355), and leave the raw regexp filter path untouched.
